stages.title: Architecture decisions, events, postbacks, BigQuery
stages.verified: ADR 0005 buffer table gives events and hours at 6.9 and 200 events/s for every failure; ADR 0007 names the dedup key (partner_id, type, transaction_id) and the HTTP answer for malformed (400), unsigned or wrong signature (401), stale (401) and unknown-click (202, quarantine) postbacks; each ADR links its requirement ids; Arthur's hand-drawn diagram (now docs/design/architecture.png) matches ADRs 0005 to 0007 after three rounds of corrections.
stages.notes: The explain-back was a diagram instead of spoken walk-throughs. It found gaps that were fixed in this commit: dead letter queue behaviour and redrive (ADR 0005), rejected/ retention and a 5-attempt limit on load jobs (ADR 0006), the loader's 9,000-file cap. Arthur decided one event per request, so the design cost is the unbatched column in nfr.md ($28.60 a month at 18M). The postback redelivery and second-purchase cases were settled while writing ADR 0007, not drawn. The ADRs were first committed in 0a66b3f; this closing commit adds the fixes.

stages.title: Data model and event catalog
stages.verified: docs/design/data-model.md: 8 CREATE TABLE statements, 9 PRIMARY KEY clauses (8 facts tables plus the MVP events table); R-3, R-4, R-10, Q-4, Q-23 and PB-5 each named in the idempotency table; every event type (prelander_viewed, step_viewed, step_answered, quiz_completed, offer_selected, offer_click, lead, purchase) appears in the trace section; grep for @ outside @example.com across docs/design, docs/testing, docs/ai and open-questions.md returns nothing. Explain-back: Arthur wrote the day 1 and day 2 flows himself (new user, Lead, return) and named the three-table query that finds the Lead.
stages.notes: Arthur designed the tables in Obsidian and the flows in text; the file was written from his drawing. His decisions: answers and email reach D1 in one POST /api/complete at quiz completion (ordering key: server receive time; per-step events are analytics only; a user who stops before the email step has no D1 rows); email through its own endpoint, never in events (the strip-in-Worker option was rejected as a special case); users row created at completion, no D1 write at entry; prelander_id trusted from the client, signed visit token deferred; table names conversions, quarantine, catalog_history; prefill between visits stays off (Q-1). Added Q-29 (Lead across prelanders of one domain). open-questions.md is now in Ukrainian for the company, with the rule recorded in CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/requirements.md. acceptance-checks.md moved to /api/complete and one event per request. A-1 reworded (2 step answers plus quiz_completed; still 9 events). nfr.md D1 size estimate to be revisited in stage 4. AI example 07 drafted.

stages.title: Metrics, reliability numbers, extensions
stages.verified: docs/design/metrics-and-operations.md: 29 metric rows with ids M-1 to M-29, none with an empty denominator; 29 links to nfr.md; nfr.md has the p95 targets (50 / 300 / 500 ms) and the alert thresholds in a 'Set in stage 4' table and no longer lists NFR-6 or MVP-5 as unset; both extensions name select() step 1 or step 5 and a concrete table (offers.exclude_after_purchase, offer_epu_observed, conversions.payout_minor); no @ outside @example.com; 0 em or en dashes; all 15 relative links resolve. Explain-back: Arthur worked through the late-postback example himself and concluded 'two separate reports' (docs/ai/examples/08).
stages.notes: Decisions: funnel denominators are distinct users per (prelander, UTC day) with start = step 1 shown; two report views, cohort by click date with an 'as of' time and finance by postback acceptance time; latency p95 measured in the Worker (events 50 ms, selection and postbacks 300 ms), external probe from EU and US at 500 ms. The file was drafted by an Opus subagent; Fable replaced its seeded probe user with GET /__probe (no events, no cleanup exception), made an excluded-after-Purchase offer behave like a disabled one (rule 3) instead of a vanished Lead, and noted 18M Workers requests as an upper bound. Also in this commit: the company's 2026-10-30 answer (no separate design review, one delivery) recorded in plan-history, requirements PRC-1/PRC-2, CLAUDE.md and the plan; stage 7 retitled. Open items: DES-5 decision-table rows live in the metrics file until implemented; Checkly free-tier limits to check; Analytics Engine sampling and Cloudflare notification types to confirm during implementation.

The old docs/ai/examples/06-diagram.png was deleted and example 06 now points to docs/design/architecture.png. design.md drafted by an Opus subagent; Fable fixed the report endpoint name, the plan file name, removed an invented email-shaped-string filter and a UserID log test, aligned the postback signature header in acceptance-checks.md with ADR 0007.
